svg.title: Music PWA — complete system architecture
svg.desc: Layered architecture showing React PWA, Supabase, Jamendo API, and Groq recommendation engine

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What goes in the Home screen of the music app?')
sendPrompt('How does the genre browse screen work?')
sendPrompt('How does the search screen work with Jamendo?')
sendPrompt('How does the library and downloads screen work?')
sendPrompt('How does the player UI work with streaming?')
sendPrompt('How should I manage global state in the music app?')
sendPrompt('How does offline caching work for a PWA music app?')
sendPrompt('What do I store in localStorage for the music app?')
sendPrompt('How does a service worker help my music PWA?')
sendPrompt('How do I set up Supabase Auth for my music app?')
sendPrompt('What Supabase tables do I need for the music app?')
sendPrompt('How do I use Supabase realtime for music sharing?')
sendPrompt('How do I use Supabase storage for downloaded music files?')
sendPrompt('How do Edge Functions work in Supabase for music?')
sendPrompt('How does Groq generate music recommendations?')
sendPrompt('How do I call the Jamendo API to get tracks by genre?')
sendPrompt('How do I get albums and artists from Jamendo?')
sendPrompt('How does Jamendo streaming URL work for audio playback?')
sendPrompt('How do I use the Jamendo radio and genre endpoints?')

svg.text: App opens → check localStorage for groq_api_key → not found: show modal → user pastes key → validate with test call → save to localStorage
Key never sent to Supabase — stays client-side only. User can update it in Settings at any time.
Supabase: fetch top 20 recently played (track_name, artist, genre) → build Groq prompt → Groq returns JSON list of
suggested genres + moods + artist names → query Jamendo with those params → display as "Recommended for you"
